title: Dimension-Free Approximate Tensorization of Quantum Hypercontractivity for Qudit Depolarizing Semigroups
authors: Yangjing Dong, Li Gao, Fengning Ou, Penghui Yao, Haigang Zhou
abstract: We prove almost tensorization for hypercontractivity and logarithmic-Sobolev constants for a class of reversible quantum Markov semigroups satisfying the positive off-diagonal scaling (PODS) property. This class includes qubit examples and generalized depolarizing semigroups with respect to full-rank states in arbitrary finite dimensions. For any such semigroup $(Φ_t)_{t\ge 0}$ and every tensor power $n$, we show that the log-Sobolev constant of the product semigroup $Φ_t^{\otimes n}$ is at least $2/(3\ln 2)$, approximately 0.96, times the log-Sobolev constant of the single-site semigroup $Φ_t$, independently of $n$ and the local dimension $d$. The proof first establishes exact tensorization of the $(q,2)$-hypercontractive inequality for integer $q$, in particular $q=3$, and then extends the estimate to all real $q>2$ by complex interpolation; the standard implication from hypercontractivity to logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities yields the stated almost tensorization result. As an application of the same method, we also obtain sharp $(q,2)$-hypercontractivity estimates for qubit depolarizing channels.
summary: The paper develops rigorous mathematical techniques to prove that certain properties of quantum evolution, specifically hypercontractivity and the Log-Sobolev constant, exhibit approximate tensorization when applied to product qudit systems. This dimension-independent result is crucial for understanding how local dynamics scale across large quantum registers.
main_problem: The primary goal is proving dimension-free approximate tensorization bounds for hypercontractivity and logarithmic-Sobolev constants in quantum Markov semigroups.
main_result: The authors establish that the log-Sobolev constant of a product semigroup scales by at least a factor of 2/(3ln 2) times the single-site constant, independent of local dimension or spectral gap.
method: The proof combines establishing exact tensorization for integer hypercontractivity parameters using complex interpolation to extend results to all real values. It relies heavily on structural properties like the Positive Off-Diagonal Scaling (PODS) condition.
model_or_system: The study concerns reversible quantum Markov semigroups ($\Phi_t$) acting on qudits of arbitrary finite dimension $d$, specifically focusing on generalized depolarizing semigroups. The analysis uses tensor products of these processes, $\Phi^{\otimes n}_t$.
key_observables: Logarithmic-Sobolev constant ($\alpha_2(L)$), hypercontractivity parameters ($p, q$), and the approximation factor $ eta \approx 0.96$.
important_parameters: The local dimension $d$ (the result is independent of it); the number of sites $n$; and the time parameter $t$.
main_assumptions: The semigroups must satisfy the Positive Off-Diagonal Scaling (PODS) property. The results are approximate ($ eta < 1$) rather than exact tensorization.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first proving specific hypercontractive inequalities (e.g., for $q=3$), then using complex interpolation to generalize these results, and finally applying these techniques to derive the dimension-independent tensorization bounds for $\alpha_2(L)$.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful tools for analyzing quantum correlations across many sites in open quantum systems, directly impacting lower bounds on entanglement measures and information processing capacity.
